The data that is being used was derived from the [TidyTuesday repository](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/tree/main/data/2024/2024-01-09). The data set for this week comes from [Statistics Canda](https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/tbl1/en/tv.action?pid=1310041501&pickMembers%5B0%5D=3.1&cubeTimeFrame.startYear=1991&cubeTimeFrame.endYear=2022&referencePeriods=19910101%2C20220101). 

### Data Manipulation
These are the libraries we will be using:
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
```
The data was downloaded from the TidyTuesday repository and is referenced here as `canada_births_1991_2022.csv`. After importing, we summarized the data by total births per year. 
```{r}
df <- read.csv("canada_births_1991_2022.csv")

yearly <- df |>
  group_by(year) |>
  summarize(total_births = sum(births))

head(yearly)
```

### Data Visualization

We will make a scatter plot of the births per year over time.
```{r}
ggplot(yearly, aes(x = year, y = total_births)) +
  geom_line(color = "darkred", size = 1.5) +
  geom_point(shape = 21, size = 3, fill = "white", color = "darkred") +
  labs(title = "Births in Canada from 1991 to 2022",
       x = "Year",
       y = "# of Births") +
  theme_minimal()
```
